lockedFacts: MERRA-2 time-averaged collections are continuous averages over the stated interval and are timestamped at the interval center
three-hourly time-averaged products are centered at 01:30, 04:30, 07:30 UTC and so on
tavg3_3d_cld_Nv (M2T3NVCLD) is 3-hourly time-averaged, model-level, 72 levels, 576x361 horizontal grid, with eight time samples per daily file
M2T3NVCLD carries CLOUD, INCLOUDQI, INCLOUDQL, QI, QL, RH, TAUCLI and TAUCLW as separate variables
TAUCLI and TAUCLW are described as in-cloud optical thickness for ice and liquid clouds
tavg3_3d_nav_Ne separately carries time-averaged model-level edge pressure PLE and edge height ZLE

distributed MERRA-2 output is postprocessed from the model cubed-sphere grid to a regular 0.625 by 0.5 degree latitude-longitude grid; the file specification states most variable collections use bilinear interpolation and names the conservatively remapped exceptions
limits: the public file specification does not state enough detail to reconstruct the conditional time-averaging behavior of an in-cloud diagnostic when a grid column is cloud-free during part of an averaging interval
time-averaged marginal fields do not by themselves provide missing cross-moments/covariances between cloud fraction, in-cloud optical thickness, layer geometry and other fields

lockedFacts: MERRA-2 is a global reanalysis, not an operational realtime weather forecast
the model is approximately 50 km scale, distributed at 0.625 degree longitude by 0.5 degree latitude with 72 native model levels
current GMAO documentation describes MERRA-2 as running behind realtime and releases data on a delayed reanalysis cadence
Earthdata CMR lists M2T3NVCLD version 5.12.4 and its DOI 10.5067/F9353J0FAHIH
GES DISC provides granule download and OPeNDAP access paths, with Earthdata authentication present in the catalog flow
limits: no M2T3NVCLD NetCDF bytes were authenticated or materialized in this bounded runtime; this cycle therefore makes no claim about actual cloud values in a specific granule

lockedUse: Karma Volume represents absorption and scattering as rates per distance travelled in the medium in m^-1
local participating-medium coefficients are evaluator inputs and are not equivalent to a coarse time-averaged path optical thickness
UE 5.8 volume materials describe local Albedo, Emissive and Extinction at positions in space
UE cloud authoring uses 3-D noise, layout and density controls to create local structure; those are renderer/authoring mechanisms rather than meteorological evidence
